body:
Reply with plain text only, no JSON, no preamble, and do not send messages to anyone else. Do not ask questions; decide.

You are drafting the lines of five short scenes for a Halloween D&D video game, "The Crooked Moon", a folk-horror campaign set in Wickermoor Hollow, a haunted valley of endless night under a giant Crooked Moon with a crone's face. The look is a Halloween that never ends, drawn like an 1980s cartoon. Each scene happens inside the Crooked House, a haunted manor on a hill above the village, while a storm has shut the party in. The house's look: sepia rot, mildew green, faded rose and teal wallpaper, bruised purple, weasels scratching in the walls, teeth clicking underfoot.

These five scenes are for the party's custom hero, a player-made character, never a named companion. The hero speaks in the FIRST PERSON as the player's own voice; there are NO Narrator lines at all, and no name appears anywhere. Each scene is a short moment of the hero meeting a sign of their own personal story inside the Crooked House. The first-person lines are plain, specific, a little haunted, two sentences at most, under about 30 words each. They must make sense for any gender and any species. Sometimes use a concrete sensory detail; never explain a secret flatly; leave the hook open. Do not invent new people, places or monsters beyond the facts given. Plain punctuation only; no em dashes, no semicolons, no brackets, no backticks.

OUTPUT FORMAT for each scene, nothing else:

SCENE duality
NODE start
PLAYER: the line
PLAYER: the line

NODE opt1
PLAYER: the line
PLAYER: the line
INSPIRE: four to seven words, past tense, no name, saying what the hero did

(then opt2 and opt3.) The start node has exactly two PLAYER rows. Each option node has exactly two PLAYER rows then one INSPIRE row. Also give the three OPTIONS texts at the top of each scene, one per line, as OPTION1: ... OPTION2: ... OPTION3: ... each under 12 words, spoken by the hero or the party, working at any hour. The third option is always a quiet way on that still completes the scene.

SCENE duality. Place: the Music Room. The hero's story: a part of them was split off long ago, taking their reflection and shadow, and now wanders the world as a double that looks just like them and commits crimes in their name. The moment: in the cracked oval mirror the hero's reflection grins when they do not, holds a bloody axe before a field of corpses, and says that sin of every kind feeds it. The options: speak to the reflection / smash the glass / turn away.
SCENE immortality. Place: the cauldron room in the attic, a round window, a floor of teeth, a great cauldron of glowing red liquid. The hero's story: they studied blood alchemy and carry a flask holding a being that has promised them first a cure and then immortality. The moment: the being in the flask goes still and then eager, recognising the pale soul-glyphs cut into the floor around the cauldron, and shows the hero how to etch the same glyphs on its vessel; the next step, it says, is blood. The options: etch the glyphs on the flask / ask the flask what it knows / cork it and move on.
SCENE kindred. Place: the master bedroom. The hero's story: a relative of theirs vanished after dreaming of the Crooked Man, a tall lanky hanged man in a bent hat with a huge yellow grin. The moment: scratched in the plaster behind the bed are the nightmares of whoever slept here, a long list in the same cramped hand; the last scratch speaks of centipedes in the deep. The options: read the scratchings aloud / trace the last scratch / leave it for now.
SCENE malediction. Place: the Library. The hero's story: a curse runs in their bloodline and only occult lore can break it; they carry a stolen page from a book. The moment: on a stand lies a heavy old tome that is half written and half blank, and the torn edge of one page matches the page the hero carries; in the margins are notes about demons that collect secrets, eyes and wings. The options: lay the stolen page against the tome / read the margin notes / close the tome and leave.
SCENE rapture. Place: the Gallery. The hero's story: they belong to a secret society that serves an otherworldly power and are a prophet of a god who seeks a foothold in a godless land. The moment: a plaque under a dour marble bust names a missionary who gathered followers to bring a god into the Hollow, and the hero feels the cold marble answer their faith. The options: read the plaque aloud / pray before the bust / walk on.
result:
SCENE duality
OPTION1: Ask the reflection what it wants from me.
OPTION2: Smash the cracked glass with my fist.
OPTION3: Turn my back on the mirror and walk away.
NODE start
PLAYER: The cracked oval glass smells of mildew and old iron, and the face inside is grinning while my own mouth stays shut. It lifts a bloody axe over a field of dead and whispers that every sin in this valley feeds it.
PLAYER: I have not cast a shadow since the day that thing tore itself loose from me. Even here, with weasels scratching behind the faded rose wallpaper, it wears my face better than I do.

NODE opt1
PLAYER: I press my fingers to the cold silvered glass and tell my double to name its price. Its lips move against mine without a sound, promising that every wicked deed in the Hollow only makes it stronger.
PLAYER: It lowers the axe and points past my shoulder toward the dark hall. Whatever it butchered out there, it wants me to follow the trail of blood.
INSPIRE: Spoke to the grinning double in the glass.

NODE opt2
PLAYER: I drive my fist straight into the grinning mouth until the rotten frame shudders on the teal wall. Shards rain down into the mildew, each piece still holding a sliver of that bloody field.
PLAYER: A dozen little mouths laugh up at me from the floorboards. Breaking the glass did not dull its axe, and it did not give me back my shadow.
INSPIRE: Shattered the mirror holding the bloody reflection.

NODE opt3
PLAYER: I turn my back on the oval frame before the thing in the glass can show me another corpse. The storm rattles the shutters, but the room behind me goes dead still.
PLAYER: I can still feel its eyes on my neck as I step toward the door. Let it starve on someone else's sins tonight.
INSPIRE: Turned away from the grinning reflection.

SCENE immortality
OPTION1: Etch the pale soul-glyphs into my flask.
OPTION2: Ask the being in the flask what it knows.
OPTION3: Cork the vessel tight and move on.
NODE start
PLAYER: Loose teeth click underfoot as I cross the attic toward the cauldron and its red glow. Inside my coat, the being in my flask goes dead still, then presses eagerly against the glass.
PLAYER: It knows the pale soul-glyphs carved into these floorboards better than I know my own pulse. It traces the shapes against my palm and whispers that after the carving comes the blood.

NODE opt1
PLAYER: I kneel by the glowing cauldron and scratch the pale floor-marks into the side of my vessel. The glass grows warm as fresh blood, drinking the red light through the round attic window.
PLAYER: The thing inside swirls faster, promising the cure I was owed and the endless years after. Now the vessel is ready, and it is waiting to be fed.
INSPIRE: Etched the pale soul-glyphs onto the flask.

NODE opt2
PLAYER: I hold the flask up to the red steam and ask how its kind came to know this house. It answers in a voice like dry teeth, saying the old alchemist here almost finished the work.
PLAYER: The glyphs on the floor were meant to trap a soul and boil it down to forever. My little prisoner says we only need blood to finish what the cauldron started.
INSPIRE: Questioned the captive being by the cauldron.

NODE opt3
PLAYER: I jam the stopper down tight and shove the warm flask back into my coat. The thing inside beats against the glass, hungry for the red light and the marks on the floor.
PLAYER: I came too far for a cure to bleed myself dry in a stranger's attic. The glyphs can wait until I know what they cost.
INSPIRE: Corked the eager flask and stepped back.

SCENE kindred
OPTION1: Read the scratched nightmares aloud.
OPTION2: Trace the last line about the deep.
OPTION3: Leave the plaster wall as it is.
NODE start
PLAYER: Behind the bedstead, the bruised purple paper is peeled back to the bare plaster, covered in a cramped hand I know by heart. Every line is a nightmare about a tall hanged man in a bent hat with a yellow grin.
PLAYER: My own kin vanished with that same crooked face burning behind their eyes. Down near the skirting board, the last scratch warns of centipedes waiting in the deep.

NODE opt1
PLAYER: I read the cramped lines aloud into the damp air, giving a voice to every bad dream my relative left in this wall. The weasels in the wainscot go quiet as the Crooked Man's yellow grin fills my head.
PLAYER: By the time I reach the last word, my throat tastes of plaster dust and old cellar dirt. Whoever slept here walked out of this room and straight down into the dark.
INSPIRE: Read the scratched nightmares aloud in the bedroom.

NODE opt2
PLAYER: I press my thumb into the lowest scratch, where a shaking nail dug deep to write of centipedes. Dried white dust clings to my skin, cold as the night outside the shutters.
PLAYER: The hand that carved this did not stop because it woke up. It stopped because something from the deep finally answered.
INSPIRE: Traced the final warning scratched in the plaster.

NODE opt3
PLAYER: I pull the tattered purple paper back over the plaster to hide that familiar handwriting. The storm groans against the roof, and the room smells of damp wool and rot.
PLAYER: Naming those dreams aloud will not bring my blood back from the dark. I know what to look for below, and that is enough.
INSPIRE: Covered the scratched nightmares behind the bed.

SCENE malediction
OPTION1: Lay my stolen page against the torn tome.
OPTION2: Study the margin notes on the demons.
OPTION3: Shut the heavy tome and leave.
NODE start
PLAYER: The heavy tome on the stand is half blank parchment, and the ragged edge of one leaf matches the stolen page in my pocket. Even the mildew green stain along the paper runs cleanly from my fragment into the book.
PLAYER: In the cramped margins, a steady hand has written of demons that gather secrets, eyes, and wings. The rot in my bloodline stirs just looking at the ink.

NODE opt1
PLAYER: I lay my stolen leaf against the torn stub, and the fibres catch like dry burrs. Faint letters bleed across the blank paper beside it, smelling of scorched feathers and old tallow.
PLAYER: The curse in my veins pulls toward the page as if it recognises its own maker. Half the spell is still missing, and something with too many eyes holds the rest.
INSPIRE: Fitted the stolen page into the torn tome.

NODE opt2
PLAYER: I lean over the stand and trace the margin notes by the dim light of the storm. These demons do not break bloodline curses for coin, only for secrets, eyes, and torn wings.
PLAYER: Whoever tore my page from this binding was trying to starve a bargain before it finished. If I want my blood clean, I now know what kind of creature keeps the ledger.
INSPIRE: Studied the demon notes in the torn tome.

NODE opt3
PLAYER: I keep my stolen page folded tight in my pocket and pull the heavy cover shut. Dust puffs from the sepia pages and settles over the stand.
PLAYER: The curse in my blood has waited generations, and it can wait one more hour. I will not read a demon's price while this house is listening.
INSPIRE: Closed the half-written tome without joining the page.

SCENE rapture
OPTION1: Read the missionary's plaque aloud.
OPTION2: Bow my head and pray before the bust.
OPTION3: Walk on through the gallery in silence.
NODE start
PLAYER: Under the dour marble bust, a tarnished plaque names a missionary who came to gather followers in this godless valley. When my fingers brush the stone, a familiar cold answers from deep inside the marble.
PLAYER: My order sent me to claim a foothold for our distant god, yet someone else tried the work before me. Behind the faded rose wall, the house settles like a congregation taking its seats.

NODE opt1
PLAYER: I speak the missionary's name and title to the empty gallery, letting the words echo past the crooked portraits. The cold marble hums against my knuckles like a struck bell.
PLAYER: My god heard that name once, before Wickermoor Hollow swallowed the flock whole. Now the stone knows a prophet has come to finish the sermon.
INSPIRE: Read the missionary plaque aloud to the gallery.

NODE opt2
PLAYER: I bow my head before the dour stone face and whisper the secret prayer of my society. Frost beads on the marble brow, and a weight presses down behind my eyes.
PLAYER: In a valley without gods, even a broken altar still holds a spark of rapture. Something beyond the Crooked Moon just looked back through the stone.
INSPIRE: Prayed before the cold marble bust.

NODE opt3
PLAYER: I draw my hand back from the cold stone and let the silence return to the gallery. The dour marble face stares out over the rotten floorboards toward the rain.
PLAYER: One prophet already vanished into the dirt of this hollow. I will keep my faith quiet until I see what ate the first flock.
INSPIRE: Left the cold marble bust in silence.
